about: Dragon Ball Z themed mods for Claude Code: Kamehameha band and gauges, Scouter, Saiyan status line, Shenron, 10 color schemes.

runs.title: First build with a nodeterm team
runs.summary: A lead and five stations built four DBZ mods (kamehameha, scouter, saiyan-status, shenron) and shared color schemes; the lead then added power gauges, the /gauges and mid-turn /grab fixes, and Shenron around the prompt.

stages.name: Lead: briefs
stages.note: specs/THEME.md, COMMON.md, one brief per mod

sessions.did: Wrote briefs, built the power gauges and hint bars, fixed goku warn, Hide (/gauges) and mid-turn /grab, added Shenron coiled around the prompt, checked try-mods.cmd live
Charge band, beam, summary, Ki gauge; 7 tests
/scouter pane, OVER 9000 toast, stamina alerts; 7 tests
Status line, transformations, /senzu, Dragon Balls (later moved to shenron); 16 tests

stages.name: Round 2 builders
stages.note: after the user asked for color schemes and Shenron

sessions.did: Shared palette in three mods, removed saiyan Dragon Balls, flagged the goku warn color
Dragon Balls, /grab, /dragonradar, /shenron art and wishes, /dbztheme; 23 tests
Fresh session with all four mods loaded; the lead read its screen: gauges, status line and hint bars drawn

events.text: User asks for progress bars for usage and context
User asks for color schemes and Shenron with 7 Dragon Balls
User lost the gauges after pressing Hide: /gauges added
User: /grab did nothing while Claude worked: commands made immediate
User asks for Shenron around the terminal border: coil over the prompt band

lessons: spawn-team is refused while the project is off screen: open stations with open-agent --run-now.
A station's headless claude -p shows NEEDS YOU (inherited hook env): a false alarm.
Give stations a reference to check copied data against; Palettes caught a wrong color by reporting it.
Every hide or close control must say how to bring the thing back.
A mod's slash command waits for the turn to end unless registered immediate: anything used mid-turn needs it.
